name: Continuum-AI-Corp__OrcaReplay
description: Read, replay and fork recorded coding-agent runs
readme:
# OrcaReplay MCP server

`orca mcp` serves six tools over stdio for reading a recorded coding-agent run.

OrcaReplay records an agent at the model-provider boundary, so a recording is the bytes the agent
actually sent and received rather than a summary it wrote about itself. The MCP server lets an
agent read those recordings.

## Tools

- `orca_list_runs` - list recorded runs
- `orca_show_run` - read one run: turns, tool calls, exit status
- `orca_checkpoints` - the points a replay can fork from
- `orca_graph` - the run as a graph; its description spells out what `recorded` and `inferred` mean
- `orca_replay` - replay the recorded run; free and offline, no provider contacted
- `orca_compare` - compare two runs; its own description states what it costs

Four of the six are read-only over the local trace store.

## Usage

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "orca": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "orcareplay", "mcp"] }
  }
}
```

## Limits

- A matching replay is not a determinism result: it proves the recorded exchange reproduces, not
  that the agent or the model is deterministic.
- Replay blocks model-provider egress only. It is not a sandbox - recorded tool calls still
  execute for real.
- The default adapter does not capture every call; embedding calls, for one, are not captured.

Apache-2.0. Node 20+. The on-disk trace format is specified separately under CC BY 4.0 in
`spec/orca-trace-v0.md`, so a recording is readable without the CLI.
